clue.text: Floral tribute to Helen?

parts.note: a garden flower whose name reads as a compliment that could be paid to Helen of Troy, the most beautiful woman of legend

explanation.surface: Someone lays flowers in honour of a woman called Helen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floral tribute' suggests a wreath; instead it is a plant whose name is itself praise. NONE-SO-PRETTY is an old country name for London pride, a saxifrage, and Helen of Troy is the obvious beauty for whom no one was so pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: An old popular name for the saxifrage London pride, which as a phrase flatters a peerless beauty like Helen.

clue.text: Going up, said "why fill a Parisian void?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the assembled letters are read from bottom to top
said tells us the word why is taken as its sound, a single letter

parts.note: the word why spoken sounds like the letter Y
taken as written
un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Someone asks, in French-flavoured puzzlement, why bother filling an empty space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up' turns the whole run Y + FILL + UN, giving the answer; 'said' makes why into the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To void a contract or ruling is to cancel it, render it of no legal force.

clue.text: A god, in the ascendant, one who writes music

indicators.note: rising, which in a down clue means the word for a writer is read upwards

parts.note: a pen is the instrument that writes
a tune is a piece of music

explanation.surface: A deity on the rise turns out to be a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the ascendant' turns PEN into NEP, which goes before TUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the Roman deity of the sea.

clue.text: Labourer turns up to wear out certain surgeons

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the whole run of letters is read upwards

parts.note: to erode is to wear away gradually
vets are surgeons, but only of animals, hence certain

explanation.surface: A workman arrives to exhaust some doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses ERODE + VETS as one run, giving STEV + EDORE. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a dock worker who loads and unloads ships, a kind of manual worker.

clue.text: Produces music for theatrical performances

definitions.meaning: to play is to perform on an instrument, as a band does

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is performing on instruments; the other is stage dramas, as at a playhouse.

clue.text: Out of print, say?

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-directory
to press is to print, as a printing press does

explanation.surface: A query about a book that is no longer in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of print' reads as one phrase about books, but splits into EX and PRESS; 'say' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words, to state it.

clue.text: To sailors, a party is not a social whirl

parts.note: taken as written
RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Seamen are told that a party is not a giddy round of social engagements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social whirl' suggests a busy party season; the italic 'social' points to a whirl that is a destructive storm instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent spinning windstorm, a whirlwind with nothing sociable about it.

clue.text: An indefinable something from over the Channel

definitions.text: An indefinable something from over the Channel

parts.words: An indefinable something from over the Channel
parts.note: a French phrase, borrowed from across the English Channel, meaning a quality that cannot quite be put into words

explanation.surface: A mysterious quality arriving from France.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes a borrowed expression: literally 'I don't know what', used in English for an elusive charm.
explanation.definitionFit: This French expression names an elusive, attractive quality that one cannot pin down.

clue.text: Disappearance of body cut into quarters

indicators.note: into tells us the word for cut goes inside the compass letters

parts.note: compass quarters: E, S and E give east-south-east
to clip is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: A corpse vanishes after being chopped into four pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' means a heavenly body, not a corpse, and 'quarters' are compass points, not four pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse is when a sun or moon is hidden from view by another heavenly object passing in front.

clue.text: Wear puts engineers into dismay

indicators.note: into shows the engineers are put inside the word for dismay

parts.note: to appal is to dismay or shock
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Something to wear horrifies the engineering team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts' is a link; 'Wear' is a noun here, clothing, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing, garments worn on the body.

clue.text: Gay to come down and listen to Edward

parts.note: to light is to descend and settle, as a bird lights on a branch
to hear is to listen
Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: An instruction to step down and pay attention to a man named Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' is used in its older sense of cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: In its traditional sense gay means merry and carefree, the same as cheerful in spirit.

clue.text: Record I preserve for a man of refinement

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
to cure meat or fish is to preserve it by salting or smoking

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a vinyl disc safe for a cultured gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person of discerning taste, especially in food and drink.

clue.text: Lady gets report on American affair

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
a report is a loud noise like a gunshot, a bang

explanation.surface: A woman hears gossip about a romance in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' suggests news; here it is the sound of a gun. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang, the whole shebang means the entire business or thing.

clue.text: Unleavened bread encountered in mazy meanderings

indicators.note: in shows the letters lie inside the words mazy meanderings

explanation.surface: Flatbread is found by wandering through a maze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meanderings' looks like an anagram signal, but the answer lies in plain view across mAZY MEanderings. 'encountered' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Azyme is an old word for unleavened bread, as eaten at Passover.

clue.text: Miss lots of balls and laugh

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls, so several of them are overs
a hoot is a burst of laughter

explanation.surface: Missing many deliveries and finding it funny.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to go past a target, to fail to hit it.

clue.text: Cunningly I entangle part of Titania's canopy

indicators.note: done with cunning, so the letters of i entangle are rearranged craftily

explanation.surface: Someone slyly tangles a piece of the fairy queen's bower.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, Titania's bank is 'quite over-canopied' with woodbine, musk-roses and eglantine.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine, the sweetbriar rose, is one of the plants Shakespeare names roofing the fairy queen's bower.

clue.text: Sort of steamer Lee wished to build

indicators.note: to build is to put together, so the letters of lee wished are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A man named Lee hoped to construct a type of steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steamer' could be a cooking pot; it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidewheel steamer is a paddle boat driven by wheels on each side of the hull.

clue.text: Called up pair outside the state of Mexico

indicators.note: outside means the word for pair goes around the telephoned word

parts.note: a duo is a pair
rang means telephoned, called up

explanation.surface: Two people were phoned while abroad in Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called up' looks like a reversal in a down clue, but it simply means telephoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Durango is one of the states making up Mexico.

clue.text: Metal animals

parts.note: a wolf is a wild animal
a ram is a male sheep, another animal

explanation.surface: Beasts made of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'animals', supplies two creatures side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is another name for tungsten, a hard metallic element (symbol W).

clue.text: Used to be heartless, the desert

parts.note: was means existed in the past, used to be

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word the is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A desert that was once cruel and without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' is a noun, a barren area, not the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: A waste is a barren, empty expanse of land, a wilderness.

clue.text: Hoping halves will show Fulham

indicators.note: halves means the first half of each of the words will, show and Fulham is taken

explanation.surface: A football supporter hopes the second half will see Fulham play well.
explanation.walkthrough: Fulham is a London football club, and 'halves' suggests the two halves of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishful describes someone longing for something, full of hope.

clue.text: Popeye's remedy for chaps in trouble

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up, so the letters of chaps in are disturbed

explanation.surface: A sailor-cartoon cure offered to men in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is fodder; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon sailor Popeye eats tins of this leafy vegetable to gain strength.

clue.text: You heard bird-song round this artist

indicators.note: heard shows the word you is taken by its sound, a single letter

parts.note: you spoken sounds like the letter U
a trill is a warbling run of birdsong
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A painter is surrounded by the sound of birds singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Utrillo was a French painter known for Paris street scenes.

clue.text: Look up and study description of antiques

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for look is read upwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: Instructions to research the history of old furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up' seems a single verb meaning research; here 'up' turns LO into OL.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden means belonging to old times, a fitting word for things long past.

clue.text: Retains in more unpleasant form

indicators.note: form means shape, so the letters of retains are put into a new shape

explanation.surface: Something keeps a nastier shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'form' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, so it means worse or more disagreeable.

clue.text: Disregarded the point about which I blush

indicators.note: about shows the words for i blush go round the compass point

parts.note: to blush is to go red, so I blush becomes I go red
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Ignoring the matter that makes me redden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, N, inside I GO RED. 'which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ignored is to be taken no notice of, overlooked.

clue.text: Men fail lamentably to arouse passion

indicators.note: lamentably means badly, so the letters of men fail are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men do badly at stirring up strong feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame is to stir up strong feeling, literally to set on fire.

clue.text: Australia captained by Cromwell

definitions.meaning: the country's formal title is the ... of Australia
the English republic of 1649 to 1660, led by Oliver Cromwell as Lord Protector, was known by this name

explanation.definitionFit: The federal union of Australian states bears this title, as did the republic Cromwell headed after Charles I's execution.
